entries.name: Home You Rent Is Being Sold
entries.summary:
The house, rooms, apartment, workshop residence, farm cottage, or other place you rent is being sold, transferred, or reclaimed by its owner.

Narrative effects: Housing uncertainty has pushed you to negotiate terms and learn quickly what other options exist nearby.

entries.name: Keeping Yourself Afloat
entries.summary:
Your current life works, but only barely. Income, food, lodging, equipment, and ordinary expenses consume nearly everything you have, leaving little room for mistakes or long-term plans.

Narrative effects: Living close to your limits has made you disciplined about ordinary needs and highly conscious of prices, terms, and what can be negotiated.

entries.name: Last Hope of the Household
entries.summary:
For practical, emotional, financial, political, or social reasons, your household increasingly looks to you as the person most likely to solve its problems.

Narrative effects: Being relied upon has strengthened your ability to make decisions and continue functioning under sustained expectation.

entries.name: Living From Job to Job
entries.summary:
You have been surviving through temporary jobs, short contracts, casual labor, seasonal work, favors, or whatever opportunity appears next rather than one stable occupation.

Narrative effects: You are accustomed to negotiating short-term work and moving wherever the next practical opportunity happens to be.

entries.name: Local Reputation on the Line
entries.summary:
How your immediate community views you now matters to your work, relationships, future opportunities, or ability to remain where you are.

Narrative effects: You are practiced at defending your standing while tracking what people actually say and believe about you.

entries.name: Lost Your Lodging
entries.summary:
The place where you were living is no longer available because of eviction, closure, conflict, sale, damage, changed terms, or another immediate disruption.

Narrative effects: Housing loss has forced you to think quickly about where else you can go and what terms might secure another place.

entries.name: Healer for Hire
entries.summary:
You provided healing, first aid, salves, minor magic, recovery care, or emergency treatment for coin, favors, lodging, or obligation.

Narrative effects: You know people become honest about pain faster than they become honest about payment.

entries.name: Hidden Agent
entries.summary:
You served, knowingly or reluctantly, as a hidden agent for a noble, faction, temple, guild, rebel cell, criminal group, foreign power, or unknown patron.

Narrative effects: You know how to make a role look ordinary while carrying a second purpose underneath.

entries.name: Household Servant
entries.summary:
You worked in an ordinary household as a servant, maid, footman, cleaner, kitchen helper, laundress, groom, general domestic worker, or whatever combination the household could actually afford.

Narrative effects: You understand that households reveal rank and character through routines long before anyone makes a formal declaration.

entries.name: Hunter and Trapper
entries.summary:
You hunted or trapped for meat, hides, pest control, trade, local obligation, or simple necessity. Tracks, trails, feeding signs, weather, patience, wounded animals, and knowing when not to take a shot mattered more than heroic wilderness stories.

Narrative effects: You read animal movement through small disturbances and know that patience often matters more than pursuit.

entries.name: Inn and Tavern Worker
entries.summary:
You worked in an inn, tavern, alehouse, roadside lodging, guesthouse, or similar place where food, drink, beds, travelers, locals, deliveries, arguments, and money passed through the same rooms.

Narrative effects: You notice who pays promptly, who expects special treatment, who is passing through, and which conversations are becoming everyone's problem.

entries.name: Junior Administrator
entries.summary:
You worked as a junior clerk, office assistant, permit handler, temple recorder, guild functionary, palace aide, or town administrator. You learned that paperwork is not glamorous, but it decides who gets permission.

Narrative effects: You sort chaos into names, dates, seals, permissions, and who forgot to sign.

entries.name: Junior Court Clerk
entries.summary:
You worked as a junior clerk in a court, noble office, palace hall, judgment chamber, diplomatic bureau, or household record room.

Narrative effects: You notice who gets written down, who gets ignored, and who asks for the record to change.

entries.name: Leatherworker's Journeyman
entries.summary:
You work as a trained leatherworker or journeyman producing and repairing belts, bags, tack, clothing, armor components, straps, cases, and other goods from prepared hide.

Narrative effects: You judge leather by treatment, thickness, stitching, wear, and whether the workmanship matches the price being asked.

entries.name: Left Home Recently
entries.summary:
You recently left home to seek work, training, adventure, patronage, independence, answers, or a life larger than the one waiting behind you. The road still feels new, and home is close enough to hurt.

Narrative effects: You still measure new places against the home you recently left behind.

entries.name: Livestock Hand
entries.summary:
You worked with cattle, sheep, goats, pigs, poultry, working animals, or other ordinary livestock. Feeding, herding, fencing, births, sickness, escape, weather, and predators were practical concerns rather than rustic scenery.

Narrative effects: You notice restless animals, weak fences, poor feed, approaching weather, and people who have never actually handled livestock.

entries.name: Local Messenger
entries.summary:
You carried messages, notices, parcels, requests, small deliveries, or warnings around a village, district, cluster of farms, estate, or nearby settlements. Your routes were local enough to become familiar rather than true long-distance courier work.

Narrative effects: You remember local routes by landmarks, households, shortcuts, bad dogs, flooded paths, and who usually has something that needs carrying.

entries.name: Haunted by Nightmares
entries.summary:
Nightmares repeatedly disturbed your childhood sleep. Their cause may have been fear, memory, imagination, stress, supernatural influence, or nothing anyone ever understood.

Narrative effects: You are practiced at regaining control after waking frightened. This trait does not establish prophetic, magical, or externally caused dreams unless another part of the story does.

entries.name: Hidden Mark Whispered About
entries.summary:
A mark, scar, birthmark, physical feature, or strange sign associated with you became the subject of quiet adult speculation during childhood. You may or may not know what they believed it meant.

Narrative effects: You are sensitive to rumors about marks, omens, bloodlines, curses, and hidden significance without assuming any of those explanations are true.

entries.name: Kept Little Collections
entries.summary:
You collected coins, buttons, stones, shells, bits of glass, feathers, cards, ribbons, foreign trinkets, or some other category of small objects and took their differences seriously.

Narrative effects: Small variations in material objects catch your attention, especially when one example seems unusual within a familiar group.

entries.name: Knew Every Alley
entries.summary:
You explored the streets, lanes, passages, courtyards, shortcuts, stairs, and back routes of your childhood surroundings until you knew how they connected better than many adults.

Narrative effects: Dense settlements quickly become mental maps for you, and you naturally notice routes that avoid the most obvious streets.

entries.name: Learned Best by Doing
entries.summary:
Explanations made more sense once you could touch the task yourself. You preferred trying, adjusting, rebuilding, copying a demonstrated motion, or learning through practical mistakes.

Narrative effects: You understand practical objects best through use and quickly notice when your own work differs in quality from a successful example.

entries.name: Learned to Keep Secrets
entries.summary:
Someone trusted you with information you were not supposed to repeat, or circumstances taught you that not every truth should be spoken immediately. You learned early that silence can protect as easily as it can deceive.

Narrative effects: You are comfortable withholding information and sensitive to the emotional reasons people entrust secrets to someone.

entries.name: Listened at Doors
entries.summary:
Closed doors made you curious, especially when adults lowered their voices behind them. You developed a childhood habit of lingering nearby and listening for conversations not meant for you.

Narrative effects: You instinctively listen for muffled conversations and know how to remain unobtrusive while doing so.

entries.name: Listened to Elders
entries.summary:
You genuinely enjoyed listening when older people talked about how places, families, customs, work, wars, rulers, roads, or communities used to be.

Narrative effects: You value lived memory as a source of historical understanding while remembering that personal recollection can be biased or incomplete.

entries.name: Little Performer
entries.summary:
Songs, jokes, mimicry, little plays, dramatic stories, dances, or attention-seeking displays were part of your childhood personality. An audience, even a tiny one, made things more exciting.

Narrative effects: You are comfortable presenting yourself to others and understand how expression can change an audience's mood.

entries.name: Lonely Dreamer
entries.summary:
You spent long stretches alone imagining distant places, impossible adventures, invented companions, future lives, or elaborate stories no one else could see.

Narrative effects: Imagination comes easily when you have enough quiet, and you are comfortable turning private ideas into stories or expression.

entries.name: Loved Cooking
entries.summary:
You enjoyed helping prepare meals, tasting ingredients, stirring pots, kneading, chopping safe foods, tending simple fires, preserving ingredients, or watching meals transform through preparation.

Narrative effects: Food preparation feels intuitive, and you pay attention to flavor, ingredients, timing, and how preparation changes them.

entries.name: Loved Crowds and Festivals
entries.summary:
Markets, festivals, processions, fairs, celebrations, performances, crowded squares, and public gatherings energized you rather than overwhelming you.

Narrative effects: You are comfortable expressing yourself in public environments and naturally absorb the customs surrounding communal celebration.

entries.name: Lucky Child of the Household
entries.summary:
People around you came to think of you as fortunate. Perhaps things simply went well when you were involved, perhaps you survived several unlikely moments, or perhaps the household enjoyed assigning good luck to someone.

Narrative effects: You understand how favorable reputation can become self-reinforcing when people want to believe someone brings good fortune.

entries.name: Healer's Waiting-Room Child
entries.summary:
You spent much of childhood around a healer's rooms, clinic, apothecary, charitable ward, or household where sick and injured people regularly waited for help.

Narrative effects: Visible signs of injury and illness stand out to you, and simple medical routines feel familiar without implying formal healer training.

entries.name: Hungry Street Child
entries.summary:
A significant part of childhood involved finding food, warmth, shelter, or useful scraps in streets and public places when there was never quite enough waiting at home.

Narrative effects: You instinctively notice overlooked supplies, discarded necessities, and places where someone can remain unobtrusive.

entries.name: Inn Yard Child
entries.summary:
You spent childhood in the yard of an inn or coaching house, around horses, wagons, carts, harnesses, travelers, deliveries, stable work, and constant arrivals.

Narrative effects: Working animals and ordinary road vehicles feel naturally connected in your experience.

entries.name: Irrigation Field Child
entries.summary:
Ditches, channels, gates, fields, water schedules, embankments, pumps, or other systems for directing water through farmland were part of your childhood surroundings.

Narrative effects: You understand the relationship between cultivated land and simple systems built to control water.

entries.name: Kitchen Runner
entries.summary:
You spent much of childhood in kitchens, pantries, sculleries, dining halls, or food stores, carrying dishes, fetching ingredients, moving messages, and learning to stay out of the way of busy workers.

Narrative effects: Food preparation environments feel familiar, and you are practiced at moving quickly through busy working spaces.

entries.name: Library Corner Child
entries.summary:
A library, archive, reading room, school collection, or book-filled corner became one of your favorite places to spend time. You learned where information lived long before formal scholarship became serious.

Narrative effects: Collections of written material feel navigable, and you naturally expect books and records to preserve information about communities and customs.

entries.name: Lumber Camp Child
entries.summary:
Timber, saws, axes, draft animals, stacked logs, forest roads, rough shelters, river transport, and hard physical labor surrounded your childhood.

Narrative effects: Forested working environments feel familiar, and you understand that useful timber depends on both environmental knowledge and physical effort.

entries.name: Heavy Blades Specialist
entries.summary:
You are trained with greatswords, oversized blades, heavy cleavers, and other large cutting weapons whose effectiveness depends on reach, commitment, balance, and controlled momentum. You know how to make their weight work for you without letting it control the fight.

Narrative effects: You constantly account for reach, swing space, momentum, and the moment when a heavy blade can turn one opening into a decisive exchange.

entries.name: Heavy Breaker
entries.summary:
You specialize in overwhelming hard defenses with large blades and blunt force. Your training emphasizes committed power, guard breaking, armor pressure, structural damage, and choosing the kind of heavy weapon best suited to what must be broken.

Narrative effects: You look at shields, armor, barricades, and stubborn defenses as structures with limits rather than as reasons to stop attacking.

entries.name: Lance Specialist
entries.summary:
You specialize in lances used from mounts, understanding couching, bracing, alignment, reach, impact timing, recovery, and how the movement of both rider and mount changes a strike. This does not by itself make you an expert rider outside combat.

Narrative effects: When mounted, you think in lines of approach, impact timing, reach, and whether the mount's movement will carry the lance cleanly through the target line.

entries.name: Light Blades Specialist
entries.summary:
You specialize in knives, daggers, short blades, and other light edged weapons that reward speed, precision, concealability, and close control. Your training emphasizes quick changes of angle, compact attacks, off-hand use, and precise weapon handling rather than raw weight.

Narrative effects: Small blades feel natural in your hands; you notice grip changes, concealed angles, openings at close range, and how little movement a precise attack really needs.

entries.name: Hardy Frame
entries.summary:
Your natural build strongly favors endurance, resilience, recovery, and resistance to physical strain. Grants +8 Constitution.

Narrative effects: You conserve effort, absorb discomfort without dramatics, and remain functional after others begin to slow.

entries.name: Heightened Awareness
entries.summary:
Your strongest mental faculty is exceptional awareness of surroundings, behavior, danger, tracks, changes, and concealed threats. Grants +8 Perception.

Narrative effects: Your attention moves constantly across sound, motion, posture, gaps, disturbed objects, and anything that does not fit.

entries.name: Instinctive Power
entries.summary:
You combine physical power, leverage, and force with awareness, observation, pattern recognition, and subtle cues in nearly equal measure. Grants +4 Strength and +4 Perception.

Narrative effects: You tend to approach difficult situations by bringing physical power, leverage, and force and awareness, observation, pattern recognition, and subtle cues together rather than relying on either aptitude alone.

entries.name: Iron Will
entries.summary:
Your defining inner strength is exceptional resolve against fear, pain, temptation, magical pressure, mental exhaustion, and attempts to break your purpose. Grants +8 Willpower.

Narrative effects: You steady yourself internally before reacting and continue acting from chosen purpose even when emotion or pressure turns severe.

entries.name: Keen Intuition
entries.summary:
Your mind strongly favors awareness of subtle cues and changing circumstances, supported by enough reasoning to test first impressions. Grants +6 Perception and +2 Intelligence.

Narrative effects: You usually lead with awareness, observation, pattern recognition, and subtle cues, calling on memory, structured reasoning, theory, and technical understanding to support that strength when the situation demands it.

entries.name: Healer's Line
entries.summary:
Healers, herbalists, midwives, physicians, battlefield medics, caretakers, or other people who tended the sick recur through your family history. Family stories remember difficult births, stubborn fevers, bad winters, old remedies, and the people who survived because someone stayed beside them.

Narrative effects: You pay attention to illness, injury, exhaustion, useful plants, and the practical care people need after heroic moments are over.

entries.name: Herbalist Line
entries.summary:
Herbalists, gatherers, remedy makers, root workers, plant sellers, or people known for useful preparations recur through your family history. Knowing what grew where mattered, but so did drying, storing, combining, and preparing it correctly.

Narrative effects: You inherited familiarity with useful natural ingredients and with the practical preparation needed to turn gathered material into something usable.

entries.name: Hunter's Line
entries.summary:
Hunters, trackers, trappers, foresters, scouts, gamekeepers, or other wilderness workers recur through your family history. Trails, spoor, animal behavior, weather, patience, and knowing when not to pursue became inherited lessons.

Narrative effects: You look for tracks, feeding signs, disturbed vegetation, silence, wind, and the small evidence that tells you something passed nearby.

entries.name: Infamous Family Name
entries.summary:
Your family name is remembered for scandal, betrayal, cruelty, treason, disaster, cowardice, corruption, or another notorious legacy. You did not commit the deeds that created the reputation, but strangers may decide how they feel about you before you ever speak.

Narrative effects: You notice recognition turning into suspicion and have learned how inherited reputation shapes conversations before you have done anything personally to deserve it.

entries.name: Innkeeping Tradition
entries.summary:
Your family repeatedly kept inns, taverns, hostels, boarding houses, roadside rooms, or other places where strangers expected food, shelter, information, and a measure of hospitality. Family reputation often depended on remembering people and settling ordinary disputes before they became expensive ones.

Narrative effects: You are familiar with reading tired or difficult guests and with the constant negotiation hidden inside hospitality, credit, prices, favors, and repeat custom.

entries.name: Landless Laborer Line
entries.summary:
Generations of your family survived primarily by selling their labor rather than owning the land, workshop, vessel, or business that employed them. Harvests, hauling, construction, loading, digging, seasonal work, and whatever else paid were recurring realities.

Narrative effects: You understand the physical cost of manual labor and the importance of negotiating what that labor is worth when ownership and security belong to someone else.

entries.name: Legal and Scribe Tradition
entries.summary:
Your family has generations of scribes, clerks, advocates, record keepers, notaries, petition writers, or people trusted to put obligations into words. Documents, signatures, seals, copies, and exact phrasing are treated as practical tools rather than decorative bureaucracy.

Narrative effects: You read agreements for omissions, ambiguous wording, witnesses, dates, signatures, and the difference between what someone intended and what they actually wrote.

entries.name: Locksmith Line
entries.summary:
Locksmiths, key makers, lock repairers, security craftsmen, or makers of small mechanical closures recur through your family history. Pins, wards, springs, fitting, worn keys, broken mechanisms, and the trust involved in controlling access were familiar subjects.

Narrative effects: You understand the construction of ordinary locks and inherited some practical familiarity with how locking mechanisms can be manipulated when necessary. This legacy does not make criminal intent automatic.

entries.name: Historian
entries.summary:
You have studied wars, migrations, dynasties, political changes, disasters, discoveries, social shifts, and the long chains of consequence that shaped modern Arkenfell. Your expertise includes comparing remembered history with surviving records rather than treating every famous story as settled truth.

Narrative effects: You connect present events to older precedents, surviving records, forgotten agreements, and patterns that people may be repeating without realizing it.

entries.name: Legal Scholar
entries.summary:
You have studied law as it is embedded in cultures and institutions: rights, punishments, contracts, inheritance, marriage, property, testimony, trade, local jurisdiction, and formal procedure. You understand that laws differ between realms and that knowing a rule is not the same as having authority to enforce it.

Narrative effects: You listen for jurisdiction, precedent, records, witnesses, obligations, and the difference between what custom expects and what an institution can actually compel.

entries.name: Lineage Scholar
entries.summary:
You specialize in noble and dynastic lineage, heraldry, succession, marriage alliances, branch families, legitimacy disputes, inherited titles, family scandals, and the historical relationships between houses. Your knowledge can identify plausible connections and contradictions, but it does not reveal secret ancestry without evidence.

Narrative effects: You notice names, crests, cadet branches, marriage ties, inheritance gaps, changed arms, and historical claims that do not quite fit the public family story.

entries.name: Linguist
entries.summary:
You study languages, dialects, scripts, translation, formal phrasing, idiom, accents, language change, and the relationship between speech and culture. This focus represents linguistic understanding; it does not automatically mean the character speaks every language they can identify.

Narrative effects: You listen for grammar, accent, idiom, borrowed words, register, and cultural context before deciding what a phrase means or where a speaker may have learned it.

entries.name: Healing Arcana
entries.summary:
You have a natural gift for Healing Arcana: closing wounds, easing pain, stabilizing the dying, cleansing minor conditions, and supporting natural recovery.

Narrative effects: You notice pain quickly, even when people try to hide it.

entries.name: Heroic Arcana
entries.summary: You have a natural gift for Heroic Arcana: courage, light, protective resolve, oath-strength, morale, sacred resistance, and power that answers crisis with defiance.

entries.name: Illusion Arcana
entries.summary:
You have a natural gift for Illusion Arcana: appearance, sound, attention, expectation, disguise, and perception. Your magic favors subtlety, performance, and misdirection.

Narrative effects: You notice what people expect to see, and how easy it is to let them keep seeing it.

entries.name: Light Arcana
entries.summary:
You have a natural gift for Light Arcana: ordinary and magical light, illumination, glare, color, reflection, refraction, visibility, and light-based pressure. Your magic expresses this theme instinctively, and training turns that instinct into controlled spellwork.

Narrative effects: You notice brightness, reflection, glare, and where darkness is being pushed aside.

entries.name: Lightning Arcana
entries.summary:
You have a natural gift for Lightning Arcana: charge, shock, sudden speed, stunning force, and unstable burst power. Your magic favors speed, disruption, and violent momentum.

Narrative effects: You react quickly to tension, like your body is always one heartbeat away from motion.

entries.name: Hollowmere Charter-Born
entries.summary:
You were shaped by Hollowmere's charters, toll rights, local councils, minor lords, ferries, militias, and the endless negotiation required for small states to remain independent beside stronger neighbors. Smoke magic suits a culture that survives through obscured intentions, concealed movement, signals, haze, and knowing when not to show everything at once.

Narrative effects: You instinctively ask who holds the right, who recognizes it, and what the bargain will cost. Smoke Arcana reflects Hollowmere's culture of concealment and uncertain borders without implying criminality.

entries.name: Hollowmere Merewise
entries.summary:
You were shaped by Hollowmere's wetlands, waterways, low settlements, old boundaries, local customs, and communities that have learned to live with uncertainty between land and water. Smoke magic belongs comfortably in a culture of mist, reeds, hidden approaches, ash-signals, and shifting visibility.

Narrative effects: You understand Hollowmere environments and the local customs built around them. Smoke Arcana reflects a culturally familiar way of shaping haze and concealment without defining your occupation.

facts.label: Modifiers
facts.value: Smoke Arcana +5, Natural Lore +8, Cultural Lore +8

entries.name: Hollowmere Mistroad Local
entries.summary:
You were shaped by Hollowmere's misted roads, river crossings, ferries, border tracks, half-seen approaches, and routes whose safety often depends on local knowledge. Smoke magic is culturally useful for obscuring movement, masking scent, signaling through haze, and turning familiar terrain against outsiders.

Narrative effects: You are practiced at finding routes and noticing what remains visible when weather, distance, or deliberate concealment obscures the obvious. Smoke Arcana is a regional magical foundation, not proof that you worked as a scout.

entries.name: Ironroot Deep-Hall
entries.summary:
You were shaped by Ironroot's ancestral halls, deep settlements, old roads beneath stone, guild memory, and the belief that work and obligation should survive longer than the people who begin them. Metal magic is culturally characteristic because forged material, ore, tools, fittings, and enduring construction are woven throughout hold life.

Narrative effects: You understand Ironroot ancestral memory and hold customs without assuming that you personally became a smith. Metal Arcana reflects the culture's deep familiarity with worked and unworked metal.

facts.label: Modifiers
facts.value: Metal Arcana +5, Historical Lore +8, Cultural Lore +8

entries.name: Ironroot Underroad
entries.summary:
You were shaped by Ironroot's deep roads, linked holds, tunnels, mapped passages, transport routes, and the engineering required to make movement beneath stone reliable. Metal magic is part of the material culture that keeps those roads, gates, fittings, and structures functioning.

Narrative effects: You understand routes through constructed underground environments and the systems that keep them usable. Metal Arcana reflects Ironroot culture without determining your trade.

entries.name: Ironroot Workswise
entries.summary:
You were shaped by Ironroot's great works: mechanisms, supports, gates, lifts, workshops, civic repairs, and the practical expectation that constructed systems should be understood rather than merely admired. Metal magic belongs naturally beside that engineering culture.

Narrative effects: You are comfortable with practical construction and mechanical problems. Metal Arcana is a cultural magical foundation that complements Ironroot craft without making Smithing universal.

entries.name: Lythael Courtwood
entries.summary:
You were shaped by Lythael's courtly forest culture, where old etiquette, living places, patient diplomacy, beauty, rank, and obligations carried across generations all matter. Heroic magic is remembered as part of the culture's old protective and oath-bound ideal: power given meaning by what it is used to uphold.

Narrative effects: You understand Lythael formal behavior, social restraint, and the cultural meaning hidden in ceremony and place. Heroic Arcana reflects an old cultural magical ideal rather than a claim that you are personally destined for greatness.

entries.name: Lythael Greenway
entries.summary:
You were shaped by Lythael's living roads, forest settlements, negotiated boundaries, and the quieter relationship between people and the lands around them. Heroic magic remains part of the culture, but here its ideal is expressed less through courtly display and more through protection, patience, and responsibility toward others.

Narrative effects: You read living environments and other people's needs with unusual care. Heroic Arcana reflects Lythael's cultural ideal of purposeful strength without requiring noble status or formal heroic training.

entries.name: Lythael Oathwise
entries.summary:
You were shaped by the Lythael that remembers: old vows, ancestral obligations, long-lived grievances, honored examples, and the belief that strength means little without restraint and purpose. Heroic magic fits that inheritance, carrying echoes of courage, protection, and deeds expected to mean something beyond the moment.

Narrative effects: You take old commitments and historical precedent seriously and are practiced at controlling immediate impulses in favor of longer obligations. Heroic Arcana is culturally inherited magic, not a prophecy about your future.

entries.name: Hard Bargainer
entries.summary:
You have deliberately learned to combine Bargaining and Appraisal as one working discipline instead of treating them as unrelated skills. The overlap gives you options that depend on both kinds of competence and grants the signature ability Count the Hidden Cost.

Narrative effects: Treat Hard Bargainer as a genuine hybrid specialization. The character combines Bargaining with Appraisal when both materially matter to the approach; do not let either skill substitute for the other or bypass normal tools, authority, resources, evidence, positioning, or consequences.

entries.name: Healing Arcana Mastery
entries.summary:
You have trained Healing Arcana beyond simple affinity into a major specialization. Your control is more precise, economical, and reliable inside its established domain, but mastery does not expand what the Arcana governs or remove mana costs, opposition, risk, or story consequences. This mastery grants the signature ability Shared Recovery.

Narrative effects: Treat Healing Arcana as a major specialization. Favor deliberate, technically informed expressions of the authored Healing Arcana domain; do not reinterpret it as another Arcana, grant effects outside its definition, or waive normal mana, strain, witnesses, and consequences. The character may use Shared Recovery when its fictional setup is plausible; it is a mastery technique, not automatic success or permission to exceed the Arcana domain.

entries.name: Heroic Arcana Mastery
entries.summary:
You have trained Heroic Arcana beyond simple affinity into a major specialization. Your control is more precise, economical, and reliable inside its established domain, but mastery does not expand what the Arcana governs or remove mana costs, opposition, risk, or story consequences. This mastery grants the signature ability Unbroken Banner.

Narrative effects: Treat Heroic Arcana as a major specialization. Favor deliberate, technically informed expressions of the authored Heroic Arcana domain; do not reinterpret it as another Arcana, grant effects outside its definition, or waive normal mana, strain, witnesses, and consequences. The character may use Unbroken Banner when its fictional setup is plausible; it is a mastery technique, not automatic success or permission to exceed the Arcana domain.

entries.name: High Argent Palatine
entries.summary:
You have formally accepted the modern Crown-recognized inheritance of House Fenrisard-Argenwald and now hold the title of High Argent Palatine. The title carries responsibility for Varglund, its dependent lands, the Valenreach-facing approaches to Argent Gate, and the surviving public obligations attached to the house. It grants lawful status and authority, but does not instantly repair the estate, remove hostile occupants, settle disputed lands, command every retainer, or make the Runed Argent Fang recognize you as First Fang.

Narrative effects: The character has formally accepted the Fenrisard-Argenwald inheritance and is the lawful High Argent Palatine under the Crown of Valenreach. Crown officials and subjects familiar with the title should address and treat the character as a high-ranking territorial noble with the legal rights and obligations attached to the office. The title provides a valid basis for issuing estate instructions, presenting claims, appointing lawful household officers, and representing the holding before the Crown. It does not automatically create practical control where occupants, divided retainers, unpaid personnel, local resistance, or rival legal proceedings remain. It also does not grant the Argent Seat until that office is formally activated, and it does not make the character First Fang without the order's separate recognition.

entries.name: High Argent Princeps
entries.summary:
You have accepted the ancestral dignity of High Argent Princeps, the pre-Valenreach title carried by the rulers of the Argent territories before their incorporation into the kingdom. It represents the ancient hereditary charge associated with Argent Gate, the founder's legacy, and the oldest traditions of House Fenrisard-Argenwald. The dignity survives alongside the modern title of High Argent Palatine, but does not by itself grant Crown office, council authority, possession of lost regalia, or command of the Runed Argent Fang.

Narrative effects: The character holds the ancestral dignity of High Argent Princeps. NPCs familiar with the old history, the Runed Argent Fang, Argent Gate, or the senior traditions of House Fenrisard-Argenwald should recognize this as a genuine inherited dignity rather than a decorative secondary title. Traditionalists may attach greater emotional or ceremonial importance to the Princeps than to the modern Palatine office, while Crown-focused figures may emphasize that it must operate within Valenreach's present legal structure. The title represents the ancient charge but does not automatically grant the Argent Seat, recover missing regalia, open every ancestral ward, create practical estate control, or complete recognition as First Fang.

entries.name: Holder of the Argent Seat
entries.summary:
You have formally activated and assumed the Argent Seat, the Crown council position attached to the Fenrisard-Argenwald inheritance. You may now appear, speak, petition, and vote through that office according to the laws and procedures governing the council. The seat grants political standing and access, but it does not guarantee agreement, influence, funding, or favorable rulings.

Narrative effects: The character has completed the formal process required to assume the Argent Seat and is recognized as its current lawful holder. Crown councillors, court officials, clerks, petitioners, and politically informed nobles should treat the character as entitled to the access, precedence, speech, petition, and voting rights attached to that seat. The office should create opportunities for formal political action and also attract scrutiny, lobbying, expectations, and opposition. It does not force other council members to support the character, guarantee that petitions succeed, provide unlimited access to restricted information, or resolve the estate's financial and territorial problems without further action.

entries.name: House Servant
entries.summary:
You worked as a servant, attendant, cleaner, runner, valet, maid, porter, or household helper. You learned how much power moves through people others barely notice.

Narrative effects: You know which rooms matter because of who is allowed to enter them.

entries.name: Hunger Arcana
entries.summary:
You carry a rare resonance with Hunger Arcana, awakened through deprivation, predatory magic, cursed appetite, relic influence, supernatural exposure, or story consequence. Hunger Arcana governs need, craving, consumption, emptiness, pursuit, draining pressure, and the dangerous moment when lack becomes power.
